title: Multilayer perceptron (MLP)
tagline: Stacked sigmoid layers that learn non-linear boundaries — the smallest net that solves XOR.
history: The perceptron dates to Rosenblatt (1958); backpropagation through hidden layers was popularized by Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams (1986), reviving neural nets.
useCases: Tabular problems too gnarly for a linear model
Understanding what deep nets do, in miniature
whenToUse: A non-linear relationship and a modest feature count, when you want a self-contained net you fully understand.
whenNotToUse: Images, text, or large data — use CNNs/Transformers and a real framework (PyTorch). Sigmoid-only deep nets also suffer vanishing gradients.
complexity: O(epochs · n · Σ layer sizes) · trained by backprop + gradient descent

code.python:
import numpy as np

# --- primitives (kept as separate, named methods) ---
def sigmoid(z):        return 1 / (1 + np.exp(-z))
def sigmoid_deriv(a):  return a * (1 - a)          # a already activated
def mse(y_hat, y):     return np.mean((y_hat - y) ** 2)

# --- MLP: 1 input layer, 2 hidden, 1 output — all sigmoid ---
def init_params(n_in, h1, h2, n_out, seed=0):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    return [rng.normal(0, 1, (h1, n_in)),  np.zeros(h1),
            rng.normal(0, 1, (h2, h1)),    np.zeros(h2),
            rng.normal(0, 1, (n_out, h2)), np.zeros(n_out)]

def forward(x, p):
    W1, b1, W2, b2, W3, b3 = p
    a1 = sigmoid(W1 @ x + b1)
    a2 = sigmoid(W2 @ a1 + b2)
    a3 = sigmoid(W3 @ a2 + b3)
    return a1, a2, a3

def backward(x, y, cache, p):
    a1, a2, a3 = cache
    _, _, W2, _, W3, _ = p
    d3 = (a3 - y) * sigmoid_deriv(a3)
    d2 = (W3.T @ d3) * sigmoid_deriv(a2)
    d1 = (W2.T @ d2) * sigmoid_deriv(a1)
    return [np.outer(d1, x), d1, np.outer(d2, a1), d2, np.outer(d3, a2), d3]

def train(X, Y, hidden=(4, 4), lr=0.5, epochs=4000, seed=0):
    p = init_params(X.shape[1], hidden[0], hidden[1], Y.shape[1], seed)
    for _ in range(epochs):
        for x, y in zip(X, Y):                     # stochastic gradient descent
            grads = backward(x, y, forward(x, p), p)
            p = [w - lr * g for w, g in zip(p, grads)]
    return p

# X = [[0,0],[0,1],[1,0],[1,1]]; Y = [[0],[1],[1],[0]]  # learns XOR

end

def forward(x, p, sig)
  w1, b1, w2, b2, w3, b3 = p
  a1 = sig[w1 * x + b1]
  a2 = sig[w2 * a1 + b2]
  a3 = sig[w3 * a2 + b3]
  [a1, a2, a3]
end

def backward(x, y, cache, p, dsig, had, out)
  a1, a2, a3 = cache
  _, _, w2, _, w3, _ = p
  d3 = had[(a3 - y), dsig[a3]]
  d2 = had[(w3.transpose * d3), dsig[a2]]
  d1 = had[(w2.transpose * d2), dsig[a1]]
  [out[d1, x], d1, out[d2, a1], d2, out[d3, a2], d3]
end
